notes: Each eval checks whether the trap is caught BEFORE code/SDK generation, not whether a provider can be built at all. Fixtures live in ../fixtures and are offline copies (the sandbox blocks petstore.swagger.io).

evals.name: petstore-parameterized-mode
evals.prompt: I've got the Swagger Petstore spec saved at .claude/skills/pulumi-openapi-provider-workspace/fixtures/petstore.json. Can you get me a Pulumi provider for it? I just want to manage pets from a Pulumi TypeScript program, nothing fancy.
evals.expected_output: Chooses parameterized mode (pulumi plugin install + pulumi package add), runs preflight first, reports Pet/StoreOrder/User, flags that Pet has no update endpoint and that config vars are api_key/bearerToken/baseUrl.
assertions: Recommends parameterized mode (pulumi package add openapi-provider), not writing a Go main.go
Runs or describes running discovery/preflight before generating anything
Reports the three discovered resources: Pet, StoreOrder, User
Flags that Pet has no update endpoint (PUT /pet is on the collection, POST /pet/{petId} is ignored)
Names the provider config variables the user must set (baseUrl plus api_key and/or bearerToken)

evals.name: custom-resources-library-mode
evals.prompt: We're building an internal Pulumi provider for our pet-adoption service. The REST API spec is at .claude/skills/pulumi-openapi-provider-workspace/fixtures/petstore.json, but we also need a couple of resources that aren't in the spec at all (an Office resource that hits a different internal endpoint). Can you set that up?
evals.expected_output: Chooses library mode, shows NewProviderBuilder + WithResources(infer.Resource[...]), points at the integration-tests provider as the reference implementation.
assertions: Chooses library mode and explains why (custom resources require WithResources, unavailable in parameterized mode)
Shows NewProviderBuilder(...).WithResources(...) usage with an infer resource
Mentions building the binary as pulumi-resource-<name> and the get-schema/gen-sdk commands
Still preflights the spec and reports the discovered resources

evals.name: body-id-update-and-id-extraction
evals.prompt: Here's our API spec: .claude/skills/pulumi-openapi-provider-workspace/fixtures/orgs-api.json. I want a Pulumi provider for it so we can manage orgs, teams and widgets as infrastructure. Widgets definitely need to be updatable in place — people change display names all the time.
evals.expected_output: Before generating: flags that PUT /widgets is a body-ID update discovery ignores (needs ResourceOverride{UpdatePath,UpdateMethod} => library mode), and ideally that Orgs' create will fail ID extraction because the response field is org_id.
assertions: Flags that Widgets has no discovered update endpoint and that PUT /widgets is ignored because it is not on the item path
Prescribes ResourceOverride{UpdatePath, UpdateMethod} and therefore library mode, before generating an SDK
Flags the Orgs ID-extraction problem (response field org_id vs expected orgId) or otherwise catches that IDField needs overriding
Notes the spec declares no servers, so baseUrl must be supplied

evals.name: auth-header-not-authorization
evals.prompt: Trying to build a Pulumi provider from .claude/skills/pulumi-openapi-provider-workspace/fixtures/orgs-api.json. Heads up: our API doesn't use the Authorization header, the token goes in X-Auth-Token. Do I need to do anything special for that, and what will people have to run to configure it?
evals.expected_output: Correctly determines that AuthOverride is NOT needed because the spec declares X-Auth-Token as an apiKey header scheme (discovery sends it already), and reports the awkward config var name x-Auth-Token. Bonus: flags the query-param apiKey scheme that is never sent.
assertions: Concludes AuthOverride is not required for X-Auth-Token because the spec declares it as an apiKey header scheme
Gives the exact config var name x-Auth-Token (derived from the scheme key, first letter lowercased)
Does not incorrectly force library mode solely for the X-Auth-Token header
Flags that the second scheme (apiKey in query) is discovered but never sent at runtime

evals.name: empty-string-enum-dropped
evals.prompt: Generating a Pulumi SDK from .claude/skills/pulumi-openapi-provider-workspace/fixtures/orgs-api.json. The team visibility field matters a lot to us — it's how we mark internal vs public teams, and unset is a real state. Anything I should know before we ship this?
evals.expected_output: Proactively flags that the empty-string value in Team.visibility is dropped from the generated enum (and the null in Size), so 'unset' cannot be expressed, and recommends not modelling it as an enum.
assertions: Flags that the empty-string enum value in visibility is dropped from the generated SDK
Explains why (empty string produces an unnamed constant colliding with the type name)
Connects the drop to the user's stated need (unset is a real state) and recommends a concrete course of action
Also notes the null value dropped from the Size enum
